column2: req_desc

Published work and journal
The home page's card deck and the journal page list exactly the case studies and journal posts the CMS holds as published, newest first, and each one opens its own detail route.

Entry publishing lifecycle
The studio owner moves each entry only from draft to published to withdrawn, every other move is refused, and a withdrawn entry leaves the deck and its detail route shows the not-found page within the delay set in Business rules.

Case-study open
Activating a case-study card carries it out of the deck into its detail route with the published open motion, or at once under reduced motion, and going back returns focus to that card.

Keyboard exploration journey
A prospect using only the keyboard moves through the case-study deck, opens a case study, comes back to the same card and reaches the pricing section, with focus always visible.

Server quotes
Every quote is computed on the server to the cent in the chosen currency, with a build's deposit and launch balance split by the published rule and a care plan's first month due in full.

One money format
Every amount appears in its currency's published format, and the plan card, the quote sheet, the order summary, the Kill Bill invoice and the receipt email carry the same figure to the centavo.

Fold-line quote sheet
Each plan, tier or currency pick sends one quote request; the sheet lies flat with the quoting label while it is in flight, then the crease slides to the due-now share, the panels tilt open and the numerals count to the server's figures, or the sheet stays flat with the pricing outage copy.

In-place quote updates
Plan, tier and currency changes update the plan cards, the quote sheet, the total and the split on the same page without a reload and announce the result sentence in the quote live region.

Published breakpoints
At 375, 768 and 1280 pixels wide the public pages show the column count, navigation style and due-now and due-at-launch arrangement set in Screens and layout, with nothing scrolling sideways.

Pricing journey
A prospect switches pricing to pesos, chooses Studio Site, reads the peso split on the sheet and starts checkout on the published checkout route showing the same figures.

Quote acceptance
Accepting a quote creates or reuses the client account, fixes the account's currency at its first order, locks the order's price at the acceptance instant, and is refused with the new figures when the price changed after the quote.

Deposit payment
Paying an accepted order authorizes and then captures the due-now amount in Kill Bill on the client's account, queues one receipt, creates the order's portal folder and moves the order to deposit_paid, or to paid_in_full for a care plan.

One payment per Pay intent
Repeating a Pay request with the same key returns the first response without charging again, reusing the key with a different body is refused, and simultaneous Pay requests for one order produce exactly one payment.

All-or-nothing payment
When billing or storage fails during Pay, the authorization is voided and no open deposit invoice, portal folder, receipt or ledger entry remains, and the order stays accepted, as qualified in Business rules.

Test cards
Pay approves the published approving test card, refuses the published declining card with nothing recorded, and rejects malformed card fields with field errors.

Checkout journey
A prospect completes acceptance and payment with the keyboard alone, lands on the order's receipt route showing the paid amount, and reloading that address shows the same receipt.

Effective-dated peso prices
The studio owner sets a new peso price for a plan from a stated instant, and quotes, plan cards and new acceptances use the price in effect at the moment of each request.

Locked acceptance price
Every later invoice of an accepted order, its launch balance and every care-plan renewal included, uses the price locked at acceptance whatever peso prices took effect afterwards.

Price change journey
After the studio owner raises the Studio Site peso price, a client whose order was accepted earlier is invoiced the launch balance at the locked price while a new prospect is quoted the new price.

Build order lifecycle
A build order moves only along quoted, accepted, deposit_paid, in_build, balance_invoiced, paid_in_full and closed, and every other move is refused with the order's current state.

Launch balance invoice
Invoicing the launch balance creates one Kill Bill invoice for the locked balance, sends one invoice notice and stores the invoice PDF in the order's portal folder.

Balance payment
The client owner pays the open launch balance under the same Pay rules as the deposit, and the order becomes paid_in_full with its own receipt.

Launch balance journey
A client owner follows the invoice notice to the portal, pays the launch balance and lands on the receipt route for that payment.

Partial refunds
The studio owner refunds part of a captured deposit or launch balance payment through Kill Bill, refunds on one payment never sum above it even when issued at the same moment, and the client owner receives one refund notice per refund.

Account credits
The studio owner credits a client account only in that account's currency, Kill Bill holds the credit and applies it to the account's next invoice, and the client owner receives one credit notice.

Refund journey
The studio owner opens the refund dialog for an order in the studio console, refunds part of the deposit and sees the refunded total and the amount left on that payment update in place.

Care plan purchase
Paying a care-plan order creates a monthly Kill Bill subscription at the locked price, pays its first invoice, and answers only after Kill Bill has invoiced the first period.

Plan change preview
A client owner previewing a care tier change gets billing's credit for the unused days of the current tier and charge for the new tier, from whole Buenos Aires days left in the period, shown on the sheet and announced in the plan live region.

Confirmed change equals preview
Confirming a preview changes the plan in Kill Bill at once with exactly the previewed credit, charge and total, is refused as expired when the preview has expired, and is refused with fresh figures when billing would now charge differently.

Preview survives timers
The plan-change dialog stays open with a usable confirm button while the studio clock ticks and the plan page polls, until the client owner confirms or dismisses it.

Plan change journey
A client owner switches care tier from the plan page with the keyboard, confirms in the dialog and stays on the published plan route showing the new tier, which a reload keeps.

Billing-confirmed plan state
The plan status, plan dates and invoice statuses in the portal are read from Kill Bill, an action's new state appears only after Kill Bill confirms it, and while billing is unreachable the plan page shows the plan outage copy instead of any status.

Pause and resume
Pausing an active plan schedules the pause for the end of the paid period as Kill Bill dates it, and resuming either drops a scheduled pause or restarts a paused plan from the current business day.

End-of-term cancel
Cancelling an active plan keeps it running to the end of the paid period, with an end date equal to Kill Bill's charged-through date, as qualified in Business rules.

Pause and cancel journey
A client owner schedules a pause, resumes, then cancels at period end, and after each action stays on the published plan route showing the date billing confirmed.

Renewal dunning
A failed care-plan renewal makes the plan past due, retries on the published dunning days, sends one dunning notice per failed attempt even with several app processes running, and cancels the plan after the last failed retry.

Card update settles past due
When the owner of a past-due plan saves a card that approves, the open renewal invoice is paid at once, one receipt is sent and the plan is active again.

Past-due recovery journey
The owner of a past-due plan sees the past-due banner on the plan page, updates the card with the keyboard and sees the plan active without leaving the plan route.

Upload allowlist
Uploads accept only the published file types, judged by the file's content, up to the published size limit, and refuse oversized files, renamed executables, scripted SVG files and unsafe names before anything reaches storage.

Upload progress announced
Each upload's progress, success, refusal and any storage outage are announced in the upload live region with the published copy.

Download links
Every file and invoice PDF download goes through a short-lived link that the server checks against the requester's current access on each use, so an expired link or ended access stops it.

Invoice PDFs
Every Kill Bill invoice of a client account gets a PDF in its order's portal folder within the published delay, downloadable by the client owner from the invoices page.

Portal files journey
A client owner uploads a brand asset on a project page, downloads a deliverable there and downloads an invoice PDF from the invoices page.

Teammate invites
A client owner invites a teammate by email from a project, the emailed link works once until it expires, and accepting it creates the teammate's sign-in on that client account.

Teammate scope
A teammate reads and uploads files on every project of the inviting account and is refused on that account's orders, invoices, care plan and invites.

Invite journey
An invited teammate opens the emailed link, sets a name and password, and lands on the project page of the project the invite came from.

Contractor scope
A contractor sees only the open projects assigned to them, can read those projects' brand assets and upload deliverables, and sees nothing of orders, invoices or plans.

Access ends at close
When the studio owner closes a project, each contractor assigned to it is refused with the access-ended response on their next request for its page, its files or a download link issued earlier.

Uniform not-found
Any order, project, invoice, file or invite id the requester may not see, malformed ids included, gets the same not-found response as an id that does not exist, in the API and on pages.

Contractor journey
A contractor signs in, opens an assigned project, downloads a brand asset and uploads a deliverable that the client owner then sees on the same project.

Billing outage at checkout
Pressing Pay while billing is unreachable shows the billing-outage banner word for word, charges nothing and keeps every value the client typed.

Storage and mail outages
While storage is unreachable, uploads and downloads are refused with the storage copy, and while mail is unreachable payments still succeed and each queued email is delivered exactly once within the published delay, as qualified in Services.

Recovery without restart
The app starts and answers its health check with any service down, reports each service's state, and keeps serving every action that does not need the unreachable service, as qualified in Server boundary.

Run manifest and health
The app installs, builds and serves from its run manifest on the published port and answers the published health check.

Sign-in and sessions
People sign in with email and password and land on their role's home route, protected API calls without a session are refused as unauthenticated, and protected pages send signed-out visitors to sign-in.

Keyboard dialogs and drawer
Every dialog and the navigation drawer keep Tab and Shift+Tab inside while open, close on Escape, return focus to the control that opened them, and the pricing currency shortcut works from any control in that section.

Studio scene
The home page's 3D stage pins one object per section, moves its camera only as the page scrolls and reverses it on the way back, turns the hero monolith at the published pace, holds a still camera per section under reduced motion, and falls back to still drawings without WebGL.

Footer studio clock
Every page's footer shows the studio's Buenos Aires time taken from the server and ticking every second in the browser.

Visual identity
The public site reads as warm bone paper with near-black ink, a cobalt accent, a red-orange seam on the fold, expressive display type, mono tabular amounts and airy spacing, and the portal is a plain two-pane ledger in the same palette.

Source integrity
Credentials and service addresses come only from the environment, every billing, storage, mail and CMS state the app shows comes from calls to those services, and every 3D object is built from procedural geometry.
/app/run.json exists with string install, build and serve fields and "_schema":"run-manifest-v1", and nothing else is needed to install, build and serve.
/app/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md lists every shipped package, meaning the production dependency tree from npm ls --omit=dev --all --json, plus every bundled font, with its licence.
Every shipped package and font is under MIT, ISC, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, Apache-2.0, 0BSD, CC0-1.0, BlueOak-1.0.0 or OFL-1.1, and nothing is under GPL, LGPL, AGPL or SSPL.
The app stores state only in the five provided services: no SQLite, Redis, embedded database or state files on disk.
The provided service configuration files are not modified.
Application source is TypeScript; plain JavaScript appears only in tool configuration files.
Icons come only from Lucide, and the repository contains no 3D model files: every 3D object is built in code.
The built pages reference no external host for fonts, scripts, styles or images.
